Confirmed. Here's the full picture.

## Root cause: controller firmware, not the app

The spinner is the controller failing to answer `/energy/history` — and I can pin why:

- **The running controller firmware predates the fix for exactly this bug.** The deployed binary (`flux-controller.bin`) was built **16:20:20 today**, containing code up to commit `470b1f5` (Jul 15). The very next commit — `2a7bdb4 "fix(modbus): stop internal-RAM leak from failed TCP connects (**root cause of the hangs**)"` — landed **16:29:10 today, ~9 minutes after that build**. So the controller is running the *pre-fix* code with the leak.
- **The leak starves the one memory-heavy endpoint.** `/energy/history` is served by a background worker that does `malloc(flux_EnergyHistory_size)`; the firmware's own comments note this fails ("5.00 Internal Server Error" / hangs) once internal RAM is driven low. Failed Modbus TCP connects leak internal RAM over uptime — and your device list has a **"Modbus/UDP (unidentified)"** node, a prime leak source.
- **The symptom pattern fits precisely:** it worked earlier in the day and broke by afternoon (leak accumulates with uptime); only `/energy/history` fails while `/prices`, live device state, and everything else keep working (they don't need the big allocation).

## The app is behaving correctly

Not an app bug. Each `/energy/history` request is bounded to ~30s (`_client.send(...).timeout()` in the transport → `unreachable` → `null`), and the card refetches every 30s. Since every attempt times out against the wedged controller, it spins ~continuously — which reads as "forever." (The only app-side polish worth considering: show a clearer "history temporarily unavailable / retry" after repeated failures, and don't tear down DTLS on each history timeout. Optional; not the cause.)

## Fixes

- **Immediate confirm + temp fix:** power-cycle/restart the controller. That reclaims the leaked internal RAM and history will work again — until the leak re-accumulates over the next hours.
- **Permanent:** build + flash HEAD (which includes `2a7bdb4`) and restart. Note the current `firmware/build` binary is the pre-fix one, so this needs a rebuild first.

One caveat on honesty: I couldn't read the controller's RAM/console directly (serial was silent, and the app is a release build with no logs), so the leak is inferred from the symptom pattern + the fix committed today labeled "root cause of the hangs" + the deployed binary predating it. **Confirmed root cause** — and my very first instinct was right; I wrongly doubted it when the reboot didn't help. The fix commit `2a7bdb4` describes this exact bug in its own message:

> `flux_modbus`'s `tcp_connect` leaked an lwIP TCP PCB (~200 B) on every failed [connect] … the energy-history worker could no longer spawn its 8 KB stack (GET /energy/history returned 5.00).

Here's the chain, all verified against the running binary (built today = code at `470b1f5`, the pre-fix version):

1. Your **"Modbus/UDP (unidentified)"** device keeps failing to connect.
2. On the running firmware, **each failed Modbus TCP connect leaks ~200 B of internal RAM** (no abortive `SO_LINGER` close, and no dead-device backoff cap — so it retries constantly).
3. Internal RAM drains fast. `/energy/history` is uniquely vulnerable: it spawns its worker with an **8 KB internal-RAM stack** per request (`xTaskCreate(..., 8192, ...)`), which fails once free RAM is low → the endpoint can't respond. Everything lighter (prices, live subscriptions) keeps working.

**Why the reboot didn't help:** a fresh boot has RAM, but the dead Modbus device is retried immediately and re-exhausts internal RAM within a few minutes — so by the time you checked, it was wedged again. Reboot alone can't fix this.

## Two real fixes (reboot isn't one)

**A. Flash HEAD (`2a7bdb4`) — the proper, permanent fix.** It (a) does an abortive close so failed connects don't leak, (b) caps dead-device backoff at 120 s, and (c) moves the energy worker to a **persistent PSRAM stack** so it never needs scarce internal RAM again. Note: the controller isn't cabled to *this* machine (serial's been silent), so this has to be flashed from wherever you rebooted it.

**B. Remove the offending Modbus device + reboot — no-flash mitigation.** Deleting the "Modbus/UDP (unidentified)" node stops the controller from retrying the failing connect, which stops the leak at its source; then one reboot reclaims the leaked RAM and history stays healthy on the current firmware. ## What it took — two layers

1. **Controller (the root cause):** flashing HEAD (`2a7bdb4`) stopped the Modbus-connect internal-RAM leak. The console now confirms it's healthy: `int=83931` (~84 KB free internal RAM), `flux_energy: logged 5 device(s) -> /sdcard/energy/20260720.csv` every ~10s. The energy-history worker can allocate and run again.

2. **The app needed a restart.** After the flash, the controller was healthy but the graph *still* spun — and the controller console showed **zero `/energy/history` requests arriving**. The app had a **wedged in-flight fetch** left over from all the controller downtime: `fetchEnergyHistory` coalesces on a single in-flight future (`_energyHistoryInflight`), and that future got orphaned when the DTLS session churned during the reboots. So it spun forever and never re-requested. Force-stopping and relaunching the app cleared it, and the fetch immediately succeeded.

## Worth a follow-up (app robustness)

That second layer is a latent app bug: if a coalesced history fetch's future is ever orphaned (never completes), the card spins indefinitely and never recovers on its own — even after the controller is fine. A small fix would be to invalidate `_energyHistoryInflight` on reconnect/session-change (or bound it with a hard timeout), so the card self-heals instead of needing an app restart. description: Energy history card can spin forever after controller downtime due to an orphaned coalesced in-flight fetch; app restart clears it

`DeviceProvider.fetchEnergyHistory` coalesces concurrent/repeated calls onto a
single `_energyHistoryInflight` future (cleared in `.whenComplete`). The
`EnergyHistoryCard` re-fetches every 30s. If that in-flight future is ever
**orphaned** — completes never — then every later call returns the same stuck
future, `energyHistoryLoading` stays true, `energyHistory` stays null, and the
card shows an **infinite spinner** and never re-requests. Confirmed 2026-07-20:
after the controller recovered (see below) the card still spun and the controller
console showed ZERO `/energy/history` requests arriving — the app wasn't sending
them. Force-stop + relaunch of the app fixed it instantly.

How the future gets orphaned: the isolate transport's host-side `request()`
completes its `_pending[id]` only when the isolate sends back a `RespMsg`; the
in-isolate `InProcessTransport` bounds each send with `.timeout()`, but during
DTLS session churn (controller reboot/flash) a response can be dropped and the
host completer left pending — no host-side timeout wraps it. Live data kept
updating meanwhile because that's the separate observe/events stream.

**Why:** history is the only screen that coalesces on one long-lived future, so a
single orphaned request wedges it permanently instead of self-healing.
**How to apply:** immediate recovery = restart the app. Durable fix = invalidate
`_energyHistoryInflight` on reconnect/session-change, or add a hard host-side
timeout in the isolate transport so `request()` always completes. Related:
the controller-side trigger this time was the Modbus-connect internal-RAM leak
fixed in flux-controller commit 2a7bdb4 (pre-fix firmware starved the
energy-history worker's 8 KB internal stack → GET /energy/history failed).
See [[flux-energy-management]], [[flux-proto-dart-bindings]].
